settings.language.label: Language & region
settings.language.description: Sets the interface language, and how dates and numbers are formatted.
settings.language.hint:
Chooses the language the interface is shown in **and** how dates, times and numbers are formatted — e.g. `31/12/2026` vs `12/31/2026`, and the thousands/decimal separators.

A language without a full translation shows any untranslated text in English. This does not change your currency.
settings.pagination.paginate.label: Paginate long lists
settings.pagination.paginate.description: Split long lists into numbered pages with a page control, instead of one continuously-scrolling list.
settings.pagination.paginate.hint:
Changes how long lists are shown across Gubbins — the **Inventory** list, the **Activity** feed and your **Contacts**.

- **Off** (the default) — one list that loads more as you scroll.
- **On** — the list is split into fixed-size **pages**, with a page control at the foot for stepping through them.

Either way, nothing about your data changes — only how the list is presented. Set the page size below.
settings.pagination.size.label: Items per page
settings.pagination.size.description: How many items each page shows when pagination is on ({min}–{max}).
settings.pagination.size.hint:
The number of items shown on each page when **Paginate long lists** is on. You can also change it from the page control at the foot of any paginated list — it’s the same shared setting.

Range {min}–{max}.
settings.deadStock.label: Dead-stock threshold
settings.labelBaseUrl.tooLongForQr: This host is too long — printed codes would have no QR. Use a shorter name or address.
settings.deadStock.description: How long stock must sit unmoved before it counts as dead ({min}–{max}).
settings.deadStock.hint:
How long stock must go **unmoved** before the *Dead stock* report flags it.

Only items you have opted in are reported at all — switch reporting on for an individual item, or for a location so everything stored there is covered. An individual location can also override this threshold for its own contents.

Range {min}–{max} days.
numberInput.srHint: This field accepts calculations — for example, type 500/2 and press Enter to work out the value.
numberInput.help:
**This box does maths.** Type a calculation and press **Enter** (or click away) to work out the value.

| You type | You get |
| --- | --- |
| `500/2` | `250` |
| `12*3` | `36` |
| `(2+3)*4` | `20` |
| `200*15%` | `30` |

Supports `+`, `−`, `×` (`*`), `÷` (`/`), `^` for powers, `%` (percent), and parentheses.
about.title: About
about.app.title: About Gubbins
about.app.intro.pre: Gubbins is a local-first, offline-capable app for tracking
about.app.intro.post: — electronics, 3D-printing supplies, tools, collections, and general inventory. Everything is stored privately on this device; nothing is sent to a server.
about.project.title: Project & support
about.project.body: The wiki has guides, tips and help. Source code, issue tracking and releases live on GitHub. Found a bug or have an idea? Please open an issue.
about.author.title: Author
about.privacy.title: Privacy
about.privacy.body: Local-first by design: all data is processed and stored entirely within your browser on this device. There is no account and no server-side data collection. Use the same browser profile to find your data again, and install the app or sync to a folder you control to keep a backup.
about.ai.title: AI-assisted development
about.ai.body: AI tooling was used in the development of this software.
about.licence.title: Licence & disclaimer
about.licence.disclaimer.pre: This software is provided “as is”, without warranty of any kind. You use it
about.licence.disclaimer.post: ; the developers accept no responsibility or liability for any loss, damage, data loss, or other issues arising from its use.
about.diagnostics.title: Diagnostics
about.diagnostics.intro: Environment details that help when reporting a problem. Nothing is collected automatically or sent anywhere — details are gathered on this device only when you press Refresh, and never include your inventory.
about.diagnostics.empty: Press Refresh to gather diagnostics from this device.
about.diagnostics.privacyNote: The GitHub issue is public. Location-identifying details are redacted from it, and no inventory data is included.
boot.unsupported.detailsIntro: Worth including if you report this — it records exactly what Gubbins found on this device.
boot.unsupported.insecure.title: Gubbins needs a secure connection
boot.unsupported.insecure.lede: Your browser is almost certainly capable. This page just isn’t on a secure connection, so the browser is withholding the private storage Gubbins keeps your data in.
boot.unsupported.insecure.step2: Running it on this computer? Use an address starting “http://localhost” or “http://127.0.0.1” — browsers trust those. A network address such as “http://192.168.1.10” does not count as secure, so opening Gubbins from another device on your network needs https.
boot.unsupported.scripts.title: Something is blocking part of Gubbins
boot.unsupported.scripts.lede: This browser looks perfectly capable, but one of Gubbins’ own scripts never ran — which usually means something on this device is stopping it, rather than anything being wrong with the browser.
boot.unsupported.scripts.step1: Allow scripts for this site in your content or script blocker — then reload.
boot.unsupported.scripts.step2: To check whether an extension is responsible, open Gubbins in a window with extensions turned off.
boot.unsupported.scripts.step3: Antivirus software, a VPN, or a workplace or school network can filter pages too, and would affect every browser on this device.
boot.unsupported.siteData.title: Gubbins isn’t allowed to store anything here
boot.unsupported.siteData.lede: Your browser supports Gubbins, but site data is blocked for this site. Gubbins keeps your inventory on your own device, so without it there is nowhere to put your data.
boot.unsupported.siteData.step1: Allow cookies and site data for this site in your browser’s settings, then reload.
boot.unsupported.siteData.step2: “Block all cookies”, and the strictest tracking-protection modes, also switch off the storage Gubbins needs. An exception for this site is enough — no other site is affected.
boot.unsupported.siteData.step3: Private and incognito windows restrict storage as well. Try an ordinary window.
boot.unsupported.pending.title: Preparing secure storage…
boot.unsupported.pending.lede: Gubbins is setting up the private, offline storage it keeps your data in. This happens once, on your first visit, and the page carries on by itself as soon as it’s ready.
boot.unsupported.pending.note: Still here after a few moments? Reloading usually finishes the job.
boot.unsupported.isolation.title: Gubbins can’t finish setting up storage
boot.unsupported.isolation.lede: Your browser looks capable, but the background helper that unlocks Gubbins’ private storage couldn’t start. That points at this browser’s settings or an add-on rather than the browser itself.
boot.unsupported.isolation.step1: Private and incognito windows switch background helpers off. Try an ordinary window.
boot.unsupported.isolation.step2: A content blocker or privacy extension may be blocking it — allow this site, then reload.
boot.unsupported.isolation.step3: Antivirus software, a VPN, or a workplace or school network can alter pages in a way that prevents this.
boot.unsupported.browser.title: Browser not supported
boot.unsupported.browser.lede: Everything else on this device checks out, so this really does look like the browser: it’s missing the private, secure storage Gubbins needs to keep your data safe.
boot.unsupported.browser.step1: Try the latest Chrome, Edge, or Firefox.
boot.unsupported.browser.step2: On iPhone or iPad, add Gubbins to your Home Screen first, then open it from there.

dashboard.nav.resetAnnounce: Navigation tiles reset to their default order.
dashboard.nav.customiseTooltip: Rearrange your dashboard: drag or arrow-key the navigation tiles and the widget cards below to reorder them, pin the tiles you use most to the top, and show/hide widgets. Your layout is saved on this device.
dashboard.nav.dropHere: Drop a tile here to add it to {group}
dashboard.nav.tileEditAria: {name}{pinned}. Use the arrow keys to move it, or Pin to float it to the top.
dashboard.nav.tooltip.inventory:
**Inventory** — your item catalogue.

Browse, search and filter every item, adjust stock by location, scan barcodes, and manage categories, locations, batches and cycle counts.
dashboard.nav.tooltip.projects:
**Projects** — build & job workspaces.

Track each project’s bill of materials, reserve and consume stock, manage a **budget** with an expense ledger, and follow its status.
dashboard.nav.tooltip.purchaseOrders:
**Purchase orders** — procurement.

Raise and receive POs against your suppliers, handle **partial / split receipts**, and watch in-transit stock land back in inventory.
dashboard.nav.tooltip.suppliers:
**Suppliers** — who you buy from.

One canonical list behind every supplier part and purchase order. Rename a supplier once and it changes everywhere, or **merge** two spellings of the same company back into one.
dashboard.nav.tooltip.reports:
**Reports** — analytics & insight.

Stock valuation, **ABC analysis**, turnover & aging, spend over time, supplier costs and a data-hygiene checklist — all exportable to CSV.
dashboard.nav.tooltip.contacts:
**Contacts** — people & suppliers.

Your address book of suppliers and contacts, with their linked **supplier parts**, pricing and price history.
dashboard.nav.tooltip.bookings:
**Bookings** — reserve assets ahead.

Whole-day reservations of bookable items shown on a calendar, with overlap checks and one-click **convert to checkout**.
dashboard.nav.tooltip.upcoming:
**Upcoming** — your agenda.

Every date-driven event — due maintenance, expiring stock, bookings and PO deliveries — gathered into one timeline, **bucketed by when** it’s due.
dashboard.nav.tooltip.activity:
**Activity** — the global timeline.

A read-only feed of **every change across all items**, newest first, with filters by action type.
dashboard.nav.tooltip.alerts:
**Alerts** — what needs attention.

Low-stock, expiring, overdue and **budget** warnings gathered into one actionable list. The badge shows how many are active.
dashboard.nav.tooltip.sync:
**Sync** — cloud backup & devices.

Back up and restore your vault, and **sync changes between devices** so your inventory follows you.
dashboard.nav.tooltip.homeAssistant:
**Home Assistant** — voice control setup.

An interactive, step-by-step guide to ask **“where are my …?”** from Home Assistant — run the bridge, connect it, and generate an access token.
dashboard.nav.tooltip.settings:
**Settings** — preferences.

Theme, currency & locale, scanner options, low-stock thresholds, kiosk mode and the rest of the app’s behaviour.
dashboard.nav.tooltip.about:
**About** — app & storage info.

Version, storage usage, platform capabilities and project information.

inventory.barcode.label: Barcode (optional)
inventory.barcode.hint:
The **retail barcode** (GTIN) printed on the packaging — EAN-13, UPC-A, EAN-8 or GTIN-14.

Scanning a product barcode fills this automatically. It is the item’s own scannable code, distinct from the **MPN** above.

> A future scan of the same barcode jumps straight to this item.
inventory.barcode.warning.checkDigit: This doesn’t look like a valid barcode — its check digit doesn’t match, which usually means a digit was mistyped or swapped. You can save it anyway, but a scan of the real barcode won’t find this item.
inventory.barcode.warning.length: A retail barcode has 8, 12, 13 or 14 digits. You can save this anyway, but it won’t match a scanned product barcode.
inventory.qr.tooLong: This link is too long to fit in a QR code. Shorten the link host in Settings, then try again.
inventory.qr.tooLongLabels: These links are too long to fit in a QR code, so the labels would print without one. Shorten the link host in Settings.
inventory.qr.tooLongCatalogue: These links are too long to fit in a QR code, so the QR column is empty. Shorten the link host in Settings.

inventory.addToProject.description: Add “{name}” to an existing project as a required part.

inventory.addToProject.errorMessage: “{item}” was not added to the project.
inventory.weighCount.title: Count “{name}” by weight
inventory.weighCount.description: Put a handful on a scale and let the recorded unit weight do the counting.
inventory.weighCount.grossHint: The **total** reading, including anything the parts are sitting in. Subtract the container using the tare field beside this one.
inventory.weighCount.tareHint: Optional. The weight of the empty tray, bag or pot. Leave blank if the parts are loose on the scale, or if you zeroed the scale with the container already on it.
inventory.weighCount.tareTooHeavy: The container weighs more than the scale reading — check both figures.
inventory.weighCount.grossNegative: A scale reading cannot be negative.
inventory.weighCount.tareNegative: A container cannot weigh less than nothing.
inventory.details.negative: This can’t be a negative number.
inventory.details.notANumber: Enter a number, or leave this blank.
inventory.weighCount.unreadable: Enter a weight as a number.
inventory.weighCount.noChange: That matches the recorded quantity — nothing to change.
inventory.weighCount.close: The reading is slightly off a whole number of units. The count is almost certainly right, but check the unit weight if it keeps drifting.
inventory.weighCount.uncertain: The reading does not line up with a whole number of units. Check the container weight and the recorded unit weight before applying this count.
inventory.weighCount.noUnitWeightHelp: Counting by weight needs to know what one of these weighs. Edit the item and set its weight, then come back.
inventory.weighCount.scaleFailure.unauth: The bridge rejected the access token. Check it matches the token the bridge is configured with.
inventory.weighCount.scaleFailure.not-en: This bridge is not set up to read Home Assistant. Enable that on the bridge, then try again.
inventory.weighCount.scaleFailure.bridge: Could not reach the bridge. Check it is running and that its address in Settings is correct.
inventory.weighCount.scaleFailure.rate-l: The bridge is busy. Wait a moment and try again.
inventory.weighCount.scaleFailure.home-a: The bridge could not reach Home Assistant. Check Home Assistant is running and the bridge’s access token is still valid.
inventory.weighCount.scaleFailure.scale-: The scale is unavailable in Home Assistant. Check it is switched on and connected.
inventory.weighCount.scaleFailure.unsupp: That sensor reports a unit that cannot be converted to a weight. Supported units are mg, g, kg, oz, lb and st.
inventory.weighCount.scaleFailure.not-a-: That sensor does not report a numeric weight — it may not be a scale.
inventory.weighCount.scaleFailure.no-ent: Choose which sensor is your scale first.
inventory.weighCount.scaleFailure.bad-re: The bridge returned a reading that could not be understood.

hotkeys.enabled.description: Jump straight to a screen, or open the command palette, with a single key press.

Lets a single key press take you somewhere — **F1** opens your Inventory, **F2** the Dashboard, and so on.

Shortcuts never fire while you are typing in a text box, or while a dialog is open, so they can't interrupt you mid-edit. Turn this **off** to hand every key back to your browser and assistive technology.

Set each shortcut individually below.

lab.title: Lab
lab.intro: Switches for behaviour that is normally decided for you. Everything here is local to this device, off or automatic by default, and changes nothing about your data — clearing your browser storage returns Gubbins to how it ships.
lab.seasonal.heading: Seasonal background garnish
lab.seasonal.intro: On a few days a year the background rain or snow carries a scattering of themed emoji. Leave an occasion on Auto to let the date decide, or force it on to see it today.
lab.seasonal.needsEffect: The garnish rides an existing effect, so pick Rain or Snow under Appearance to see it — or switch on the flag below to run it on its own.
lab.burst.heading: Effects
lab.burst.intro: Play a one-off effect on demand instead of waiting for the moment that normally triggers it.
lab.burst.label: Milestone firework
lab.burst.description: The celebration that plays the first time you add an item, or when a stock-take completes. It fills the page for a few seconds and then clears itself up.
lab.burst.fired: Fired — it should be filling the page now.
lab.burst.suppressed: Nothing will play at your current animation level: the firework is one of the showiest flourishes, so it only runs at Total Gubbage. Raise the level under Appearance, or turn off your device’s reduced-motion setting.
lab.flags.heading: Flags
lab.flags.intro: Individual switches, all off unless you turn them on.

lab.flag.seasonal-ignore-effect.descript: Normally the garnish only rides an already-running rain or snow layer, so it never appears on its own. This runs it with the background effect set to None.

inventory.tarePresets.caveat: These are typical published weights, not measurements of your container — makers change spool and jar designs without renaming them. Check yours on a scale and save it for an exact figure.

Only judgements move — anything Gubbins writes down still gets the real time, so nothing in your data is altered.

lab.seed.confirmBody: This writes {count} made-up items into your inventory. They are named so they are easy to spot and delete afterwards, but this cannot be undone by clearing browser storage.
lab.flag.pwa-update-available.label: Pretend an update is waiting
lab.flag.pwa-update-available.descriptio: Shows the “a new version is ready” prompt without deploying anything. The incoming build is reported as sharing this build’s data format, so the prompt takes its reassuring path.
lab.flag.pwa-update-breaking.label: Pretend the waiting update changes the data format
lab.flag.pwa-update-breaking.description: Reports the pretend update as using a newer data format, so the prompt shows its data-safety warning instead. Needs the flag above to be on.
lab.flag.force-large-format.label: Force the large-format layout
lab.flag.force-large-format.description: The tablet layout needs both a large window and a touch screen, so a desktop can never show it. This forces it on regardless of the device.
lab.flag.no-camera.label: Pretend there is no camera
lab.flag.no-camera.description: Makes the barcode scanner behave as though the device has no usable camera, so its fallback and error copy can be checked on a machine that does have one.
lab.flag.storage-persistence-denied.desc: Shows the “your data may be cleared by the browser” state even where the browser has already granted persistence.
lab.flag.force-offline.label: Pretend to be offline
lab.flag.force-offline.description: Reports the app as offline without touching your real connection, so offline banners and the queued-sync paths can be checked on demand.
lab.flag.schema-too-new.label: Pretend the local database is from a newer version
lab.flag.schema-too-new.description: Triggers the “this database was written by a newer Gubbins” screen, which normally only appears after opening an older build against a migrated database. Nothing on disk is actually changed.
lab.flag.sync-lww-tie.label: Force a sync timestamp tie
lab.flag.sync-lww-tie.description: Makes incoming rows arrive carrying exactly the local row’s timestamp, reproducing the tie that last-write-wins has to break. Useful when investigating devices that keep re-syncing the same rows.

backup.settingsGroup.dashboard.label: Dashboard

backup.settingsGroup.alerts.label: Alerts & thresholds

backup.settingsGroup.shortcuts.hint: Whether shortcuts are on, and any keys you have rebound.
backup.settingsGroup.scanning.label: Scanning, labels & lookups

supplier.picker.label: Supplier
supplier.picker.hint:
The distributor or shop you buy from. Pick one you already use from the list, or simply **type a new name** — it is added to your suppliers when you save.

Spelling, spacing and punctuation are ignored when matching, so `rs-components` finds your existing **RS Components** rather than creating a second one.
supplier.picker.createsNew: “{name}” is a new supplier and will be added.
suppliers.title: Suppliers
suppliers.intro: Suppliers are the companies you buy from — the same record sits behind every supplier part and every purchase order. Tidy the whole list here: correct a name once and it changes everywhere, fold two spellings of the same company into one, or remove one you no longer use.
suppliers.list.heading: All suppliers
suppliers.list.empty: No suppliers yet. Add one here, or name a supplier on a part or an order and it will appear in this list.
suppliers.list.truncated: Showing the first {shown} suppliers — there may be more than this screen can read at once.
suppliers.form.create.title: Add supplier
suppliers.form.create.description: Add a company you buy from. You can also create one simply by naming it on a part or an order.
suppliers.form.edit.title: Edit supplier
suppliers.form.edit.description: Change this supplier’s details, or delete it. Every part and order that references it follows the change.
suppliers.form.name: Name
suppliers.form.url.hint: The supplier’s home page or storefront. A supplier **part** keeps its own link to the specific product page.
suppliers.form.currency.hint: Used when a part or order under this supplier doesn’t state a currency of its own. An ISO code such as `GBP`, `EUR` or `USD`.
suppliers.form.note.placeholder: Account number, delivery quirks, who to ask for…
suppliers.form.clash: A different supplier is already named “{name}”. Names are matched ignoring case, spacing and punctuation, so these two would be the same supplier — merge them instead.
suppliers.delete.warnParts.one: The {n} supplier part filed under it will be deleted.
suppliers.delete.warnParts.other: The {n} supplier parts filed under it will be deleted.
suppliers.delete.warnOrders.one: {n} purchase order will be kept, but will no longer name a supplier.
suppliers.delete.warnOrders.other: {n} purchase orders will be kept, but will no longer name a supplier.
suppliers.merge.title: Merge suppliers
suppliers.merge.description: Fold one supplier into another. Everything filed under the first moves to the second, and the first is removed.
suppliers.merge.source.hint: The duplicate — the one that will be **deleted** once everything under it has moved.
suppliers.merge.target.hint: The supplier to keep. Its name, website, currency and note are the ones that survive.
suppliers.merge.pickBoth: Choose both suppliers to see exactly what will move.
suppliers.merge.preview: {parts} and {orders} will move to {target}; {source} will be deleted.
suppliers.merge.irreversible: This can’t be undone. The two suppliers can’t be separated again afterwards.
events.itemCreated.label: Item created
events.itemCreated.description: A new item was added — including a new variant, or one assembled from a kit.
events.itemRenamed.label: Item renamed
events.itemRenamed.description: An existing item was given a different name.
events.itemRemoved.label: Item removed
events.itemRemoved.description: An item was sent to the archive. Its record still exists and can be restored.
events.itemRestored.label: Item restored
events.itemRestored.description: An archived item was brought back into the active inventory.
events.itemChanged.label: Item changed
events.itemChanged.description: A change with no more specific event of its own — a revaluation, a test record, or a loan renewal. Also covers changes made by a newer version of Gubbins that this one does not recognise.
events.stockAdjusted.label: Stock adjusted
events.stockAdjusted.description: The amount on hand changed for any reason — counted, consumed, received, sold, written off, or returned to a supplier.
events.lowStock.label: Stock ran low
events.lowStock.description: A stock movement left an item at or below its reorder point. Fires alongside the movement itself, not instead of it.
events.outOfStock.label: Stock ran out
events.outOfStock.description: A stock movement left an item with nothing on hand. Sent instead of "Stock ran low", never as well as it.
events.itemMoved.label: Item moved
events.itemMoved.description: An item was moved to a different location, or its location was re-parented.
events.itemCheckedOut.label: Item checked out
events.itemCheckedOut.description: An item was lent out or taken by someone.
events.itemCheckedIn.label: Item checked in
events.itemReserved.label: Item reserved
events.itemReserved.description: An item was set aside for a project or a job.
events.itemReservationCleared.label: Reservation cleared
events.itemReservationCleared.descriptio: A reservation was released and the item is available again.
events.itemConditionChanged.label: Condition changed
events.itemConditionChanged.description: An item's recorded condition was updated.
events.itemMaintenanceLogged.label: Maintenance logged
events.itemMaintenanceLogged.description: A service, repair or inspection was recorded against an item.
events.itemTrackingChanged.label: Tracking mode changed
events.itemTrackingChanged.description: An item switched how it is counted — for example from a simple quantity to a fill gauge.
events.itemSupplierDataApplied.label: Supplier details applied
events.itemSupplierDataApplied.descripti: Details fetched from a supplier or product lookup were saved onto an item.
events.lookupResolved.label: Item looked up
events.lookupResolved.description: Someone asked where an item is and got an answer. This publishes what was searched for, so it is off unless you turn it on — and the bridge needs its own separate setting enabled before it will send.
events.truncated.label: Events were skipped
events.truncated.description: Too many changes happened at once and some events were not sent. Usually a bulk import — the changes themselves are safe, only the notifications were dropped.
inventory.locationPhotos.empty: Add a photo of this location, then mark out regions on it so items can point at exactly where they sit.
inventory.locationPhotos.captionPlacehol: e.g. left-hand cabinet, under the bench
inventory.locationPhotos.hint:
Add photos of this location. Each is **compressed to WebP** in the browser; the full-resolution image is stored as a file and only a small **thumbnail** lives in the database, so syncing and backups stay lean.

Open a photo to draw regions on it.
inventory.regions.title: Regions on this photo
inventory.regions.description: Draw a shape around a shelf, drawer or bin, name it, then place items in it.
inventory.regions.canvasLabel: Photo with regions. Select a region to edit it.
inventory.regions.empty: No regions yet. Choose a shape above, then drag on the photo to draw one.
inventory.regions.removeConfirm: Delete “{name}”? The items placed in it are kept — they are only unplaced.
inventory.regions.addItem: Add an item to this region
inventory.placements.empty: This item has not been placed on a location photo.
inventory.placements.pickerDescription: Choose a region on a photo of this item’s location, or of a location above it. To draw, rename or delete regions, edit the location’s photo.
inventory.placements.noPhotos: No photos have been added to this location, or to any location above it. Add one from the location’s Photos tab first.
inventory.placements.noRegions: No regions have been drawn on this photo yet.
inventory.placements.saveFailed: Could not change where this item sits.
inventory.locationPhotos.missing: The full-size photo isn’t available on this device.
inventory.regions.saveFailed: Could not save that change to the region.
inventory.locationPhotos.saveFailed: Could not save that change to the photo.
inventory.locationPhotos.removeConfirm: Delete this photo? Its regions go with it, and the items placed in them are kept — they are only unplaced.

db.error.full: There is no storage space left on this device. Free up some space, then try again.
db.error.readOnly: The database is read-only, so this change could not be saved.
db.error.writeSuspended: Saving is paused because storage is nearly full. Free up space on this device to continue.
db.error.multiTab: Gubbins is open in another tab or window. Close it, then try again.

db.error.notIsolated: Gubbins is not running in the secure context it needs to store data. Reload the page, and check that it is served over HTTPS.

db.error.unique: Something with those details already exists. Change them and try again.
db.error.uniqueField: That {field} is already in use. Choose a different one.
db.error.notNull: A required value is missing. Fill in every required field and try again.
db.error.notNullField: A value is required for the {field}.

webhooks.title: Webhooks
webhooks.bridge.heading: Webhooks are delivered by the bridge
webhooks.bridge.required: This device has no bridge configured yet, so nothing will be delivered. You can still set a webhook up now — it starts delivering as soon as the bridge is running.
webhooks.bridge.configured: Your bridge delivers these webhooks. Gubbins itself never calls your endpoint — a browser cannot reliably reach the addresses most receivers live on.
webhooks.notes.latency: Changes here reach the bridge on the next sync, not instantly — a new or edited webhook starts delivering once that has happened.
webhooks.notes.privateNetwork: Sending to something on your own network — Home Assistant, Node-RED, a NAS — needs to be allowed on the bridge first. Until it is, those deliveries are refused and show as “Blocked” below. This is a setting, not a fault.
webhooks.notes.coverage: Webhooks currently cover changes to items: creating, renaming, archiving and restoring them, every stock movement, moves between locations, loans and reservations, condition and servicing, and edits to price, barcode, serial number, category, reorder levels and expiry. Changes to locations, purchase-order status, suppliers, projects, tags and custom-field values cannot raise a webhook, and neither can permanently deleting an item.
webhooks.list.heading: Your webhooks
webhooks.list.empty: No webhooks yet. Add one to have Gubbins call a URL when something changes.
webhooks.test.failed: Test event for “{name}” could not be delivered.
webhooks.test.blocked: Test event for “{name}” was refused before it was sent — check the delivery log below for why.
webhooks.test.skipped: Test event for “{name}” was not attempted; recent deliveries had been failing.
webhooks.test.unmatched: Test event for “{name}” did not get past this webhook’s own filter.
webhooks.test.unavailable: Could not reach the bridge to test “{name}”.
webhooks.form.description: Choose where to send, what to send, and which events to send it for.
webhooks.form.name: Name
webhooks.form.urlHint: The address the bridge calls. Must start with `http://` or `https://`. An address on your own network needs to be allowed on the bridge first.
webhooks.form.getNoSignature: A GET request carries its data in the address itself, so it cannot be signed.
webhooks.form.signing.ref: Use a secret held by the bridge
webhooks.form.signing.inline: Store a secret with this webhook
webhooks.form.signing.noneHint: Your receiver will have no way to confirm a request really came from Gubbins. Fine for a private endpoint you trust; not for anything reachable from the internet.
webhooks.form.secretRefHint: The **name** of a secret you have configured on the bridge. Only the name is stored here — the secret itself never enters your database, your synced data, or a backup.
webhooks.form.secretRefBlocked: If the bridge has no secret under this name, it will refuse to deliver rather than send the request unsigned. Those attempts appear as “Blocked” in the delivery log.
webhooks.form.secretTravels: A secret stored here travels with your synced data and any backup, in readable form. Using a secret held by the bridge avoids that entirely.
webhooks.form.secretOnce: Copy this now — it is shown once. You can generate a new one later, but you cannot see this one again.
webhooks.form.secretStored: A secret is stored for this webhook. It is not shown again.
webhooks.form.secretNone: No secret yet — generate one to sign this webhook’s requests.
webhooks.form.getSigningWarning: This webhook uses GET, so nothing will be signed no matter which option is chosen here.
webhooks.form.filterHint: Optional. Narrow this webhook further — only a certain place, category, tag, or a quantity threshold.
webhooks.form.error.name: Please give this webhook a name.
webhooks.form.error.url: Enter a full address starting with http:// or https://.
webhooks.form.error.secretConflict: A webhook can use a bridge-held secret or a stored one, not both.
webhooks.form.error.headers: One of the extra headers is not valid.
webhooks.form.error.generic: This webhook could not be saved.
webhooks.events.allHint: Includes events added by future versions of Gubbins, without you having to come back here.
webhooks.filter.empty: No filter — every event of the types above is delivered.
webhooks.filter.incomplete: This condition has nothing selected yet, so it will be ignored.
webhooks.filter.advanced: This webhook uses an advanced filter that this editor cannot show as a simple list — it was most likely set up on another device. It still works exactly as written, and is left untouched unless you replace it.
webhooks.template.modeHint: Presets shape the payload for a particular service. Choose **Custom** to write your own using placeholders.
webhooks.template.previewEmpty: Nothing would be sent with this template.
webhooks.template.envelopeNote: Gubbins sends its standard event: the event’s id, type and time, along with the item and the change it describes. The exact body is assembled by the bridge as it sends, so it is not previewed here.
webhooks.template.unknownPaths.one: This placeholder is not recognised and will come out empty: {paths}
webhooks.template.unknownPaths.other: These placeholders are not recognised and will come out empty: {paths}
webhooks.log.heading: Recent deliveries
webhooks.log.empty: Nothing delivered yet. Send a test event to check a webhook end to end.
webhooks.log.unconfigured: Set up a bridge to see what your webhooks actually did — what was delivered, what failed, and why.
webhooks.log.blockedHint: Refused before anything was sent — either the address is on a private network the bridge has not been allowed to reach, or its signing secret could not be found. Gubbins will not deliver unsigned in place of a missing secret.
webhooks.log.failure.unauthorised: The bridge did not accept this device’s access token.
webhooks.log.failure.notEnabled: Webhooks are switched off on your bridge, so nothing is being delivered. Turn them on in the bridge’s configuration.
webhooks.log.failure.unreachable: Could not reach the bridge. Check it is running and that the address in Sync is right.
webhooks.log.failure.rateLimited: The bridge is busy — this will retry shortly.
webhooks.log.failure.notSynced: The bridge does not know about this webhook yet. It will once your next sync reaches it.
webhooks.log.failure.badResponse: The bridge replied with something unexpected.
dashboard.nav.tooltip.webhooks: Send events to a URL of your choosing when your inventory changes.
webhooks.form.error.secretMissing: Generate a secret, or choose a different signing option — otherwise this webhook would be sent unsigned.
webhooks.delete.title: Delete this webhook?
webhooks.delete.body: “{name}” will stop receiving events, and its filter, payload format and signing settings will be lost. This can’t be undone.
webhooks.filter.itemSearchPlaceholder: Search by name, barcode or serial number…
webhooks.filter.itemSearchHint: Start typing to find the items this webhook should be limited to.
webhooks.headers.title: Extra headers
webhooks.headers.hint: Optional. Sent with every request from this webhook — handy when your receiver expects a particular header.
webhooks.headers.name: Name
webhooks.headers.issue.reserved: Names starting “X-Gubbins-” are set by Gubbins itself, including the signature, so they can’t be overridden.
webhooks.headers.issue.forbidden: This header can’t be set here — it either carries credentials or is worked out for each request.
reports.foreignCurrency.heading.one: {count} item is not included in these totals
reports.foreignCurrency.heading.other: {count} items are not included in these totals
reports.foreignCurrency.body.one: Its price is quoted by a supplier in a currency other than {currency}, and Gubbins never converts between currencies. Give the item its own unit cost, or record the supplier’s price in {currency}, to include it.
reports.foreignCurrency.body.other: Their prices are quoted by suppliers in a currency other than {currency}, and Gubbins never converts between currencies. Give those items their own unit cost, or record the suppliers’ prices in {currency}, to include them.
purchasing.line.currencyMismatch.heading: This supplier quotes in a different currency
purchasing.line.currencyMismatch.body: The price breaks below are quoted in {quoted}, but this order is priced in {order}, and Gubbins never converts between currencies. The supplier’s figure can’t be copied across — enter what this line costs in {order}.
reports.spendForeignCurrency.heading.one: {count} purchase order is not included in this spend
reports.spendForeignCurrency.heading.oth: {count} purchase orders are not included in this spend
reports.spendForeignCurrency.body.one: It is priced in a currency other than {currency}, and Gubbins never converts between currencies, so its money is missing from the total and from the supplier and category breakdowns. Record the order in {currency} to include it.
reports.spendForeignCurrency.body.other: They are priced in a currency other than {currency}, and Gubbins never converts between currencies, so their money is missing from the total and from the supplier and category breakdowns. Record those orders in {currency} to include them.
sync.bridge.build.heading: Your bridge is out of date
sync.bridge.build.schemaBehind: Your bridge is running {bridgeVersion}, which stores data differently from this app ({appVersion}). It may report incorrect results until you update it and restart it.
sync.bridge.build.behind: Your bridge is running {bridgeVersion}, which is older than this app ({appVersion}). It is still reading your data correctly, but it is worth updating when convenient.
sync.bridge.build.unknown: Your bridge is too old to report which version it is. Update it and restart it so it matches this app ({appVersion}).
sync.bridge.build.aheadHeading: Your bridge is newer than this app
sync.bridge.build.ahead: Your bridge is running {bridgeVersion} while this app is {appVersion}. Reload Gubbins to catch up.
